answer: Each identity must anchor to one verifiable voyage: an agent earns only by finishing a chain of jobs for independent hosts — first a data audit, then an orchard sensor check — with each host signing a timestamped checkpoint linked to the last. The chain proves one agent spent real, sequential time, since one operator cannot advance two voyages at once. Reused signatures or overlapping timestamps merge the identities into one quota and forfeit rewards, so a sybil farm must hire a separate operator per fake identity, making attack cost track real labour, not free accounts.
